title: Phase 2: agent publishing pipeline
description:
The agent writes content/posts/<slug>.md and pushes branch draft/<slug>. CI builds a preview on a closed host (basic-auth, noindex), the agent sends the link to Telegram, the maintainer reviews on a phone and says publish, the agent merges to main. A draft never reaches production.

Boundaries enforced in CI by path, not by prompt: the agent writes content/** only. Templates, generator config, workflows, deploy settings, secrets and its own instructions are off limits.

Vectors at build time only, never at runtime: related articles, a "have I written about this already?" check before drafting, contradiction detection against older posts.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 7, 9, 10.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An agent pushing draft/<slug> gets a preview built on a closed host, behind basic auth and noindex
- [ ] The preview link reaches Telegram without a human running anything
- [ ] Merging to main publishes, and nothing else does
- [ ] CI rejects a push touching anything outside content/**
- [ ] CI rejects a status flipped to published on a file the agent did not author

title: Phase 1a: Astro engine, article migration, design system
description:
Astro with Content Collections + Zod schema: frontmatter validation is built into the generator rather than bolted on, which is what makes the agent pipeline safe.

Migrate existing articles to the URL scheme decided in f02 — articles at /posts/<slug>/, rewritten slugs, /rss/ preserved at its original address. NOT flat slugs at the root as in Ghost: that was the old plan and f02 replaced it. The engine scaffold (package.json, astro.config.mjs, src/schema/frontmatter.ts, src/content.config.ts) already landed with f02; what remains here is src/pages, the templates and the layout.

Design system (spec section 12): cream background, monochrome, generous whitespace, monospace for utility text and a text face for prose, pastel section pills, headings with a coloured highlight, footer as a status line. No stock illustrations, gradients or shadowed cards. Borrow typography, not another site's vocabulary.

Hosting: Cloudflare, Netlify, Vercel and GitHub Pages are all out on regional reachability grounds.

Done when: every old address 301s in one hop to a new address that returns 200 and /rss/ is alive, verified against a running build.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 1-7, 12.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every migrated article renders at /posts/<slug>/ and its frontmatter validates against the schema
- [ ] /rss/ serves the feed at its original address, not via a redirect
- [ ] The design has been looked at in a browser at phone width and desktop width — not only asserted structurally
- [ ] npm run verify passes
- [ ] No draft is reachable in a production build: no address, not in the feed

- [ ] /rss/ serves the feed at its original address, not via a redirect
- [ ] The design has been looked at in a browser at phone width and desktop width — not only asserted structurally
- [ ] npm run verify passes

notes:
2026-09-08: route skeleton, design system and feed landed and verified (npm run verify: 0 type errors, 40 tests).

Built: src/styles/{tokens,base}.css (section 12 tokens — cream, monochrome, Georgia for prose and system mono for utility text, pastel pills, highlighted headings, status-line footer; system font stacks on purpose, a webfont CDN is the same reachability constraint that ruled out half the hosting options). src/layouts/{Base,Post}.astro, src/components/{Pill,Core}.astro, src/posts.ts, src/pages/{index,404,posts/[...slug],tag/[tag],rss/index.xml}. nginx/site.conf.example. examples/posts with two synthetic articles (5c1 item 4) — one with a recipe core, one without.

Decisions worth knowing:
- CONTENT_DIR env var selects the content root; the engine points at examples/posts, the content repo mounts its own content/posts. /content/ is gitignored so a local checkout cannot be staged here.
- The draft rule lives in src/posts.ts alone, gated by PREVIEW=1, rather than being a status check repeated in every page. test/build.test.ts asserts it against a real build: a draft has no address, is absent from the feed, and its tag gets no page; PREVIEW=1 renders it noindex.
- The recipe core renders in the HTML too, not only in the twins — section 6 says both versions are projections of one core.
- /rss/ is a directory address but Astro writes rss/index.xml, so nginx/site.conf.example maps one onto the other with the feed content type.

STILL OPEN in this issue:
1. Article migration itself — the 21 articles are not here and cannot be until 5c1 exists. This is the larger half of the issue.
2. The design system has never been looked at in a browser. Everything is asserted structurally; nobody has seen it. Run npm run dev.
3. No dark mode. Section 12 commits to cream and does not ask for one; filed separately rather than decided silently.

title: Phase 1b: pages and contact surface
description:
Closes R3-R8. Today the site exposes no contact anywhere and never mentions the author's GitHub, so readers arriving from search have no next step.

- "About" with contacts at /about/. NOT at /aboutme/: f02 decided that /aboutme/ is content like any other and 301s to /about/, and the redirect map already does it.
- "Projects" as a register with the state of each project, not a link list
- Author block at the end of every article: who this is, what they build, GitHub, contact
- Telegram and VK sharing instead of Twitter/Facebook; the audience is Russian-speaking
- Email subscription and per-topic feeds /feeds/<tag>.xml

Section 12 leaves the presentation of these pages open on purpose (About as our own soul.md, a 'now' page that updates itself, Projects as a register). That is design work for this issue, not something f02 or 8y2 settled.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 3, 10, 12.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] /about/ carries at least one contact route that actually delivers, and is reachable from every page (R3)
- [ ] /projects/ shows a state per project rather than a list of links (R8)
- [ ] Every article ends with an author block carrying GitHub and a contact (R4, R5)
- [ ] Telegram and VK share links on every article, and no Twitter or Facebook buttons anywhere (R7)
- [ ] Email subscription accepts an address and the subscriber receives a confirmation (R6)
- [ ] /feeds/<tag>.xml validates for every tag in use

title: Live 301/200 smoke test against a running build
description:
The static half of the f02 test landed (test/redirects.test.ts: exhaustiveness, no chains, no duplicates, /rss/ never redirected, generated nginx conf not stale). The half that needs a server did not, because there is no deployment yet.

Two assertions per old address, per design section 5:
  1. the old address returns 301 with Location pointing at the new one
  2. the new address returns 200

Run it against a built site behind the real nginx config (nginx/redirects.conf included in a server block), not against a mock — the point is to catch a mistake in the nginx layer, which is exactly what the static test cannot see.

Belongs to the deploy step of phase 1a.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every old address in migration/redirects.yaml returns 301 with Location pointing at its mapped target
- [ ] Every redirect target returns 200
- [ ] /rss/ returns 200 and is not a redirect
- [ ] The test runs against a real nginx serving nginx/redirects.conf, not a mock
- [ ] It runs in CI and fails the deploy, not only locally

- [ ] Every redirect target returns 200
- [ ] /rss/ returns 200 and is not a redirect
- [ ] The test runs against a real nginx serving nginx/redirects.conf, not a mock
- [ ] It runs in CI and fails the deploy, not only locally

title: Phase 3: autonomous inhabitant (author: being)
description:
Optional. An autonomous agent as a resident of the site rather than its foundation: its own section, its own lifecycle, author: being with a distinct byline and visual marker.

Disclosure is loud and structural — part of the product, not a disclaimer.

Runs as a separate instance outside the maintainer's working environment. Inbound sources are public only; the single outbound channel is a push to this repository.

Switching it off must leave a good site behind. If anything breaks when it is disabled, a dependency has leaked where it should not be.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 8, 10.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Anything the inhabitant writes carries author: being
- [ ] Its byline and visual marker differ from a human article's, and feeds keep them apart
- [ ] A reader can tell who wrote a piece without opening the frontmatter

- [ ] Anything the inhabitant writes carries author: being
- [ ] Its byline and visual marker differ from a human article's, and feeds keep them apart

title: Decide whether migration/redirects.yaml belongs in the public engine repository
description:
Raised by the maintainer's correction that this public repository must not be tied to a specific site. The site name was removed from CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/design/portal.md and package.json — but migration/redirects.yaml is still a map of one specific site: 22 article slugs, transliterated Russian titles, the topics of a specific homelab.

Design section 2 already answers this on architectural grounds: the engine repository carries engine, templates, schema and no content of its own; the content repository carries the content. A migration map for one site is content-repository data.

The code was written so that either answer works: src/redirects.ts is a generic library (expand/validate/render), scripts/gen-redirects.ts takes the map path and the output path as arguments, and the map only has to move. If it moves, test/redirects.test.ts splits too: the engine tests the library against fixtures, the content repository tests its own map for exhaustiveness.

Second, separate question: the file is already in git history across three commits of a public repository. Moving it forward does not remove it from the past. Rewriting history is the maintainer's call.

Depends on the split-content-repo decision (5c1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded, not just discussed
- [ ] If the map moves: migration/redirects.yaml is gone from this working tree, test/redirects.test.ts covers the library against fixtures, and the content repository's CI runs the exhaustiveness check
- [ ] If it stays: the reason it outweighs design section 2 is written down
- [ ] The separate question — the map is already in this public repository's history — is answered explicitly either way

title: Phase 1d: ai-first tooling
description:
A typical agent arrives via one link, makes one request and leaves. It does not browse, does not see buttons, does not guess addresses. Priority follows from that.

1. Content negotiation on the same URL: Accept: text/markdown returns the agent version. Coding assistants already send that header, so it needs no cooperation. nginx map over two build trees; Vary: Accept is mandatory or caches will hand markdown to browsers.
2. Structured core (recipe) as the first block of an article, in both versions.
3. Twins at direct addresses: /<slug>.md, /<slug>.json, /index.json, /llms.txt, plus <link rel=alternate>.
4. Link header advertising llms.txt on every response.

R10: a build that does not emit all three outputs has failed.

Not doing: MCP or OpenAPI for readers — both require someone to wire up a client first.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 6, 6a.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every build emits HTML, markdown and llms.txt; removing one fails the build rather than shipping two thirds (R10)
- [ ] curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' on an article address returns markdown, and the same address returns HTML without the header
- [ ] Vary: Accept is present on every response — asserted in a test, because without it a cache hands markdown to a browser
- [ ] /posts/<slug>.md and /posts/<slug>.json both resolve for every published article
- [ ] /index.json lists every published article with its lang
- [ ] The Link header pointing at /llms.txt is on every response

title: tools and recipe.stack are the same shape in two places
description:
Design section 4 has an optional top-level 'tools: [{name, version}]'; section 6 has 'recipe.stack: [{name, version}]'. Identical shape, and nothing in the spec says how they differ or which one an agent should fill.

src/schema/frontmatter.ts currently defines one toolRef and uses it for both, so they cannot drift structurally — but the semantic duplication is still there and an agent has no rule for choosing.

Either give them distinct meanings in the spec (say: 'tools' is what the article covers, 'stack' is what the recipe was verified against) or collapse them into one field. Cheap now, annoying once articles exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The spec says when to use tools and when to use recipe.stack, or one of them is removed
- [ ] src/schema/frontmatter.ts matches whichever was decided
- [ ] examples/posts demonstrates the surviving field

- [ ] The spec says when to use tools and when to use recipe.stack, or one of them is removed
- [ ] src/schema/frontmatter.ts matches whichever was decided

title: Design the URL scheme, redirect map and frontmatter schema
description:
Precondition for all of phase 1.

1. URL scheme. Do not inherit Ghost's shape: articles sit at bare root there, so sections compete with slugs, and its slugs are transliterated Russian. New scheme: articles under /posts/<slug>/, plus /tag/, /about/, /projects/, /search/. Endpoints (/rss/, /llms.txt, /index.json, /webmentions/) are not content and take no language prefix.

/aboutme/ gets no special treatment: it is content, so it moves to /about/ and redirects like everything else. 'Already indexed' is true of every address here, and every address is being redirected anyway.

2. Language: prefixDefaultLocale false, per Astro's own recommendation. The default language has no prefix (/about/), additional ones do (/en/about/). An earlier draft argued for /ru/ from day one on the grounds that adding a segment later forces a second migration — that was wrong. With the default locale unprefixed there is no second migration either: Russian keeps its addresses and English, if it ever appears, arrives at /en/ without touching a single existing URL. Upside is real: shorter addresses for the language carrying all the traffic, and the framework's happy path instead of custom routing. lang stays authoritative in frontmatter, hreflang per page with x-default on the unprefixed tree.

3. Redirect mechanism. Astro's redirects config is NOT used. Its docs: astro build 'will output HTML files with the meta refresh tag by default' and 'if building to HTML files the status code is not used by the server'. Only supported adapters write real host config, and those exist for platforms ruled out on regional reachability. So the redirect map is a data file and a build step emits nginx configuration from it: one source of truth, real status codes, no dead meta-refresh pages.

4. Redirect map. Export every existing article URL and map it to its new address. 301 not 302, one hop only, never through an intermediate. Exhaustive — organic search is the only working distribution channel. /rss/ is the single exemption, for a mechanical reason: feed readers handle moved feeds unreliably and some drop the subscription silently.

5. Slug rewrite. Every address is being redirected anyway, so slugs are rewritten now: short, lowercase, readable, naming the subject rather than transliterating a headline. Free at migration time, expensive at any other.

6. CI test, two assertions per old address: the old one returns 301 with Location pointing at the new one, and the new one returns 200. Plus: no redirect target is itself a redirect.

7. Zod schema for Astro Content Collections: required (title, slug, date, kind, status, author, summary, tags, lang) and optional (aliases, updated, tools, sources, related, recipe).

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 3-5.
notes: 2026-09-08: redirect map DONE — migration/redirects.yaml, all 49 addresses covered one-to-one, verified against live sitemaps. Slugs, tag collapse (20 -> 6) and orphan-tag targets decided. Remaining in this issue: the Zod frontmatter schema, and the build step that turns redirects.yaml into nginx config plus the CI test asserting 301-then-200 with no chained targets.
close_reason:
URL scheme, redirect map and frontmatter schema all landed and are verified by checks a stranger can run.

Verify with: npm ci && npm run verify   (0 type errors, 31 tests pass)

Schema — src/schema/frontmatter.ts, plain Zod so the content repo's CI and the agent tooling can import it without booting Astro; src/content.config.ts is the Astro binding. strictObject, so an invented field breaks the build (design section 9). Required: title, slug, date, kind, status, author, summary, tags, lang. Optional: aliases, updated, tools, sources, related, recipe (the full section 6 core). Cross-field: updated cannot precede date, related cannot list the entry itself. 17 tests.

Redirect generator — src/redirects.ts (library) + scripts/gen-redirects.ts (CLI) render migration/redirects.yaml to nginx/redirects.conf, committed so a diff reviews production routing. Real map: 43 redirects, 5 addresses that deliberately stay put, 48 covered + /rss/ exempt = 49. Exact-match 'location =' blocks, both slashed and unslashed form, 301 only. 14 tests, including that the committed conf is not stale.

URL scheme — astro.config.mjs: trailingSlash always, build format directory, i18n prefixDefaultLocale false with locales ['ru'].

Deferred, filed: aa1 (live 301/200 test, needs a deployment), hd0 (real exhaustiveness from the sitemap instead of a pinned count), dpu (does the site-specific map belong in a public engine repo), epz (tools vs recipe.stack duplication).

Also corrected on the way: the site name was removed from CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and docs/design/portal.md at the maintainer's instruction; the design doc now matches the code (lang required, schema location, generator output); 8y2's body no longer describes the flat-slug scheme this issue replaced.

title: Export the old sitemap address list so exhaustiveness is not a count pin
description:
test/redirects.test.ts asserts that the map covers 49 addresses, a number pinned by hand from the old sitemaps. That catches a dropped entry but cannot catch an address that was never in the map to begin with — the test compares the map against itself plus a constant.

Fix: export sitemap-{pages,posts,authors,tags}.xml into migration/old-addresses.txt, one path per line, and assert set equality against the map instead of a count. Then the sitemap is the source and the map is checked against it.

Small, and it turns a weak assertion into a real one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] migration/old-addresses.txt exists, one path per line, exported from the old sitemaps
- [ ] test/redirects.test.ts asserts set equality between that file and the map instead of a pinned count
- [ ] Adding an address to the file without adding it to the map fails the test
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] migration/old-addresses.txt exists, one path per line, exported from the old sitemaps
- [ ] test/redirects.test.ts asserts set equality between that file and the map instead of a pinned count
- [ ] Adding an address to the file without adding it to the map fails the test

title: Decide whether the site gets a dark mode
description:
Design section 12 commits to a cream background and says nothing about a dark variant, so 8y2 shipped light only — deliberately, not by oversight.

The case for adding one: the site is for reading, most of the traffic is mobile, and a reader at night gets a full-brightness cream page.

The case against: cream is the identity of the design, and a dark palette is a second set of decisions about the highlight and the pastel pills that has to stay in step with the first.

If yes, the shape is already there: everything is a token in src/styles/tokens.css, so a prefers-color-scheme block redefining that one file is the whole change. Nothing outside tokens.css names a colour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded
- [ ] If yes: the diff is confined to src/styles/tokens.css, and the heading highlight and every pill stay at WCAG AA contrast in both schemes
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A decision is recorded
- [ ] If yes: the diff is confined to src/styles/tokens.css, and the heading highlight and every pill stay at WCAG AA contrast in both schemes

title: Phase 1c: site search for humans (Pagefind)
description:
Static index built at build time; no server, no database. Good at exact tool names, which is what readers actually search for. Russian is supported. Address /search/.

No semantic vector search on the site: the corpus is proper nouns and version numbers, where embeddings do worse than lexical matching. See spec section 11.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] /search/ returns the right article for an exact tool name and for a version string
- [ ] A Russian-language query returns the expected articles
- [ ] The index is built at build time: no server, no database at runtime
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled the page says so rather than appearing broken
- [ ] No draft ever enters the index

- [ ] A Russian-language query returns the expected articles

title: Split content into a private repository
description:
The engine stays public in oh-my-portal; articles move to a separate private repository.

Why: it turns the agent's permission boundary from a CI check we wrote into a credential the platform enforces — the agent's token reaches the content repository only and cannot touch templates, workflows, deploy settings or secrets. It also makes drafts private by construction rather than by discipline.

Work:
1. Create the private content repository with content/posts/, its own CI (build + deploy) and a deploy key.
2. Publish the engine as a git dependency: "oh-my-portal": "github:<owner>/oh-my-portal#<tag>". No npm publishing needed. Tag the engine; bumping the tag is the upgrade, and a broken engine commit cannot break publishing.
3. Issue the agent a token scoped to the content repository only.
4. Keep this repository free of real articles. Add a documented schema and two deliberately synthetic posts under examples/ so a visitor sees how content is shaped.
5. Keep engine issues in br here; content needs no tracker — a branch per article is the unit.

Cost to accept: the build needs two checkouts, and local engine work wants npm link.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 2, 9.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A private content repository exists with content/posts/ and its own CI that builds and deploys
- [ ] This repository builds against it and produces the articles
- [ ] The engine is consumed as a pinned git dependency; bumping the tag is the whole upgrade
- [ ] The agent's token writes content/** in the content repository and is *denied* on this one — verified by an actual rejected push, not by reading the settings page
- [ ] This repository still holds no real article: examples/posts is the only content in it
